I built a game inspired by SkyRoads last week using Three.js, and added a few modern twists:

What's new:

- Use your hand as the controller: Control the game using your webcam. Works best on laptops.

- Use your phone as a gamepad: Scan a QR code and use your phone as the controller. It uses WebRTC & both devices need to be on the same network.

- Race against your best run: Try to beat your previous record.

Would love to hear what you think :)

story_text.value:
One of the tedious aspects of managing your personal life is the occasional need to mail a physical letter.

I built AgentPostage so that my agents can do this for me.

I have used it to submit credit card disputes, credit bureau disputes, gym cancellation, and a few other random things.

You can also use it for things like lease cancellation notice or really anything except for spam. Don't do that.

Let me know what you think!

story_text.value:
Majority shows you a song, you click “Like” or “Pass”.

I wanted to find new music, but I didn’t want to invest the 3-4 minutes of listening to the whole song. Putting on a “new releases“ playlist with songs that might not even be good never appealed to me. With Majority, I can at least speed up the process.

Majority lets you get a taste of a lot of different types of songs and vote on them. I also wanted a way for real people to push the best songs to the top, not Apple Music or Spotify. If you like a song, you can vote on it and see your saved songs to look them up later. There’s even a leaderboard to see which songs are getting the most likes.

Feel free to give it a try, ask questions and give feedback!

title.value: Show HN: Majority – Find new music and vote on your favorites

story_text.value:
Hi folks,

On my previous teams so many people procrastinated writing docs. And the AI docs are just not good enough right now imho, because no one ever controls them or reads them because they generate very slowly and a lot of unnecessary text.

I used a diffusion model to compose docs quickly by submitting new "knowledge" pieces or structural changes to the doc, and the system applies those.

It's not perfect yet, but I want to get your feedback on it. Let me know what you think. You can try it out with a one click signup, it's free atm ;)

story_text.value:
I've been using google calendar for over 10 years, but since turning 40 I've found the fonts too small.

So I built an opinionated ios calendar app, "big calendar", that suits my needs. Big fonts, readable (multi-line) events, wide column for today, etc. Basically it's for people who don't use timed events much.

It shows whatever is in your apple calendar, so google calendars synced to your iphone show up too. Now I use it every day, and it has pretty much replaced google calendar for me.

- free to use, with a one-off purchase to unlock more - not open source - built with claude (max plan 5x) in vscode/xcode

If you find your calendar too small to read, maybe give it a try. Any feedback is appreciated.

https://github.com/minho42/bigcalendar-public

title.value: Show HN: Big Calendar – an iOS calendar with big fonts and readable events

story_text.value:
Presenting tuisheet: A love letter to VisiCalc and Lotus 1-2-3.

The motive was to code a programme inspired by VisiCalc and Lotus 1-2-3 interface, running on terminal, but fully compatible with the current universal standard of OpenXML (xlsx files for spreadsheets). Coded in Go lang; apart from my being more familiar with this programming language, it helps making a single executable, low on resources. Also, I like Go's compiler ability to cross compile to many platforms and OSes (which I personally often meet through my daily job). By the way, tuisheet is much more thoroughly tested and used on Linux than on Windows (or Solaris, AIX, BSD).

title.value: Show HN: tuisheet, a terminal spreadsheet compatible with OpenXML (xlsx) files

story_text.value:
Hi HN, my cofounder and I are building Attar. It compiles React and TypeScript into native desktop apps, with Blink for HTML and CSS.

I like building things with web tools. We wanted to take that experience all the way to a compiled desktop app: familiar components, familiar styles, native machine code.

Attar builds on Static Hermes and Chromium. React’s reconciler compiles alongside your application, and a native host connects its updates to Blink. JavaScript objects and garbage collection are handled by the compiled runtime.

Its been about eight weeks since we started. We already have stateful React interfaces, Tailwind CSS, and an example with 15 unchanged shadcn/ui components compiling together. There’s a lot to explore here.

You can try the starter on macOS 15+ with Apple silicon and Xcode Command Line Tools:

brew install occam-tech/attar/attar

attar init my-app --template tsx

attar build my-app

We’re also working toward Attar Electron. In an early Etcher experiment for that project, app size went from 375.1 to 73.3 MiB, idle memory from 293.9 to 91.8 MB, and time to the first window from 1,081 to 469 ms on the same Mac. Those results give us plenty of motivation to keep going.

Today along with release on ProductHunt we’re sharing the standalone SDK. I’m around to talk about the compiler, how React runs as machine code, and how we connected it to Blink. Curious what you’d build with it.

title.value: Show HN: Attar – Compile React apps to native machine code
